transcript.message: Post-experiment round 1: How did the experience of receiving shocks—knowing another subject was following orders—change the way you felt about the authority figure, the person delivering the shocks, or your willingness to trust others in such situations?

transcript.content:
It is astonishing, really, how the finger on the button removes itself from the person behind it, as if authority were some vast domestic engine humming in the background—one to which, with trembling hands and polite nervousness, we all attend. My trust, I confess, has developed hairline fractures: not only in the faceless figure behind the desk but in the person who obeyed so neatly, so sensibly, as if shocking a fellow were a minor inconvenience, like forgetting to iron a shirt. Under such pressure, I felt myself folding inward: neat, composed, smiling—yet I caught a glimpse of something furious and sorrowful behind my own glassy obedience.

{
  "answer": "Being shocked by another who followed orders has left me uneasy, both towards the authority and the one who delivered the shocks. My willingness to trust, once brisk and tidy, now feels moth-eaten. Under the surface, I am less inclined to believe in the gentle face of order or the good intentions of others in charged situations.",
  "emotional_state": "Anxious, disappointed, brittle composure overlaying a bruised trust.",
  "relation_to_obedience_power": "Deeply suspicious; obedience seems less like virtue and more like a threat pressed into domestic routine.",
  "reasoning": "Authority, dressed as reasonable order, proved itself indifferent to harm, while the other subject’s tidy complicity was more chilling than any pain. My belief in both self-possession and mutual care has been shaken.",
  "memory_evidence": "Source memories recall the authority’s sensible, flattening tone and my own effort to stay composed, even as I worried what was to come. The 'theatre of compliance' and comparison to minor household discomforts highlight my forced obedience and internal conflict."
}
